title: A table several times larger than shared_buffers: cold-cache, IO-bound reads under RLS
issue: When the table does not fit in shared_buffers every extra heap page an RLS plan touches is an IO. A tenant filter that cannot be pushed into an index, or that forces a plan to read rows of other tenants, multiplies reads (see the hit/read columns).
symptom: Selective subjects behave well when an index on tenant_id is used and badly when the plan walks the primary key and discards rows; broad subjects read most of the table either way. full_count is answered by an index-only scan (the index fits in shared_buffers after warmup); heap_sum must read the 2.2 GB heap through the 1 GB pool, so its hit/read columns show real reads.

scale.meaning: rows in app.big, ~110 bytes each: 2.2 GB heap + 1.0 GB indexes (3.3 GB, 3.3x shared_buffers=1GB). Tenants = scale/5000 (4000 at default), rows of a tenant scattered over the whole heap.

subjects.name: selective
subjects.note: one tenant, ~5000 rows scattered over the whole heap

subjects.name: broad
subjects.note: half of all tenants (2000 at default scale): ~10M rows
